doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: His worst gigs
summary: Drinking-related bad nights with a rock band and complaints about loudness from managers.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well you’ve got all these great gigs you’ve played. And this is a sort of a hard question. Do you recall your worst gig ever?

Boy oh boy. There could be a whole bunch of them. A couple of gigs I learned my lesson early to not overindulge. Especially drinking. I don’t drink anymore and I never had a problem with it, I just don’t care for it anymore the way it makes you feel. A couple of times with the rock band getting a little too drunk to play and they were my good buddies, we’d played together for a long time. The piano player, Tom Hook, he’s looking at me. I’m going “I’m sorry.” He’s like, “hey get out of here.” And he finished the night by himself on piano playing Tom Waits songs and things like that. But yeah, things like that. Gigs where we were always too loud. “Turn that P.A. off.” “Well we don’t have a P.A., we’re a jazz group, we’re just playing for dancing.” “You guys are too loud. Turn that P.A. down.” “We don’t have a P.A.” There’s a microphone so they can do speeches so they can do the toast. That’s all. Things like that. “You’re too loud.” It happens all the

time. People see the drums coming in and they do not sit near the bandstand and they don’t understand that I could probably play drums quieter than anybody. You know? So worst gigs would have been more like dealing with food and beverage managers instead of the other musicians.
